transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), John (FinGuard - Head of Security), Marta (FinGuard - Platform Eng), Sana (FinGuard - CISO), Evan (FinGuard - Legal)

Summary:
Quick security and compliance review focused on data residency and region pinning. Customer wants assurance about EU-only processing for regulated PII, details on cross-border processing, sub-processors, KMS and key management, and how audit logs + RBAC/SSO work with pinned regions. Agreed next steps: send security pack, provision EU trial environment, schedule deeper technical follow-up.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO mentions, RBAC & SSO integration (SAML/Okta), audit logs and retention, encryption at rest and KMS/HSM options, data residency and region pinning, cross-border processing, sub-processor disclosures, VPC/private deployment options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey thanks everyone for joining, I, uh, appreciate you carving out the time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] John (FinGuard): Yep John here. Marta here. Evan, Sana. 
[00:11] Marta (FinGuard): Morning all.
[00:14] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya from Redwood, I'll be covering the technical side.
[00:18] Alex (Redwood): Cool, goal for today is to walk through how we handle region pinning and data residency, answer questions about cross-border processing and sub-processors, and make sure we have clear next steps.
[00:28] Sana (FinGuard): High level, we are a EU-headquartered fintech, a lot of regulated customer PII must remain in EU — can you do EU-only processing end-to-end? 
[00:36] Priya (Redwood SE): Short answer: yes, we support EU-only processing paths. We have hosted regions in eu-west-1 (Frankfurt) and eu-west-2, we also support private deployments and VPC connectors if you need network isolation. The key is pinning the route for inference to the EU region — that can be enforced at routing policy.
[00:52] John (FinGuard): How deterministic is that? I mean, if we request inference with a customer tenant pinned to EU, are there any fallback scenarios that might route outside EU in failure cases?
[01:03] Liam (Redwood SE): Great question. We have fallback policies — default behavior is to keep within region. If a node in the EU region becomes unhealthy and you have strict residency requirements, we can configure no cross-region fallback. If you need higher availability the tradeoff is having multi-region active-active; you'd have to accept cross-border replication or set up a private dedicated capacity in EU.
[01:27] Marta (FinGuard): So availability vs residency is the tradeoff, got it. Is that configurable per-tenant or per-route?
[01:33] Priya (Redwood SE): It's per-deployment/policy. You can set it at the tenant level or per-route. For example, fintech sensitive routes can be pinned with "no-fallback" and lower-priority routes can have multi-region.
[01:45] Sana (FinGuard): What about logs and audit trails? We need audit logs to be stored in EU too and retention configurable to 7 years for certain data classes.
[01:55] Priya (Redwood SE): Audit logs are stored in the same region as the deployment by default. We offer retention policies; longer retention is an add-on. We also stream logs to your SIEM via private links and you can enforce storage in your own tenant/storage bucket in EU.
[02:10] John (FinGuard): Encryption — do you support customer-managed keys, KMS, HSM? We need control over keys and the ability to rotate and revoke.
[02:18] Alex (Redwood): Yes — we offer a few options. For hosted, we support provider-managed keys by default. For enterprise/private deployments you can bring your own KMS; we integrate with AWS KMS and customer HSMs via external key manager. For EU-only keys we can ensure keys are provisioned in the EU region.
[02:33] Evan (FinGuard): Will we get logs of key usage and key rotation events in the audit trail?
[02:38] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes key usage events are logged and can be included in the audit stream. Those logs are stored in the pinned region unless you configure cross-region replication.
[02:48] Marta (FinGuard): Sub-processors — who's running things under the hood? We need a full list for our DPA and to run approvals.
[02:56] Alex (Redwood): We have a sub-processor disclosure. Core infra is on top cloud providers (AWS/GCP) plus CDN and monitoring partners. For private deployments a lot of that is under your control. We'll share the current sub-processor list and the DPA language; if there are specific disallowed sub-processors we can discuss mitigations. Link: https://redwood.ai/security/subprocessors (note: placeholder link in transcript).
[03:18] John (FinGuard): Cross-border processing: our customers explicitly prohibit any export of PII to the US. How do you handle metadata, telemetry, and debug traces — anything that could leak content or identifiers to the control plane in the US?
[03:32] Priya (Redwood SE): Important point. Our control plane is separate from data plane. For hosted customers, metadata is minimal — heartbeats, metrics. By default, nothing (no customer content) is moved outside the pinned region. For strict no-export needs, we offer private control plane options and on-prem bundles. We also support an EU-only control plane for enterprise customers.
[03:52] Sana (FinGuard): Is that an additional cost or part of the enterprise SLA?
[03:57] Alex (Redwood): Usually bundled as part of Private/Enterprise contracts. We'll include pricing in the next steps.
[04:04] Evan (FinGuard): SSO and RBAC — we use Okta and have fine-grained roles required for operators and auditors. How granular is your RBAC?
[04:12] Liam (Redwood SE): We support SAML SSO (Okta) and SCIM provisioning. RBAC supports roles aligned to operator/dev/audit roles and you can create custom roles with permissions. We also log all admin actions with impersonation and access logs for auditors.
[04:25] John (FinGuard): For auditors, can we provide time-bound access for a third-party auditor and have that recorded?
[04:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes we support temporary access tokens and time-limited roles; those actions are included in the audit trail.
[04:36] Marta (FinGuard): A technical nit: how do you guarantee model artifacts and cached KV data remain in-region? We use KV cache and prefix caching in inference workflows.
[04:45] Priya (Redwood SE): The KV cache on the serving runtime is co-located with the inference nodes. If pinned to EU, KV cache replicas live in EU. We do have optional cross-region replication for caches for active-active setups, but that is opt-in.
[05:00] John (FinGuard): Are backups encrypted and stored in EU?
[05:04] Priya (Redwood SE): Backups follow the same residency policy; we can encrypt them with your keys in the EU.
[05:10] John (FinGuard): Any third-party analytics or telemetry that might sample request content?
[05:15] Alex (Redwood): We don't send customer request content to third-party analytics. We do aggregate telemetry (latency, token counts) at a service level. For strict customers we can turn off telemetry or route it to a customer-owned endpoint.
[05:26] Sana (FinGuard): On the legal side, can you accept EU SCCs and any specific redlines around data transfers?
[05:33] Evan (FinGuard): (overlapping) We often require SCCs plus contractual assurances about sub-processors.
[05:39] Alex (Redwood): Yes we support SCCs and will work with your legal team on DPA redlines. We'll share our standard DPA and propose language for EU-only processing.
[05:47] John (FinGuard): Operational runbooks — if we need to failover or revoke keys, what's the RTO? We need an SLA on rotation + emergency key revocation steps.
[05:58] Priya (Redwood SE): For private/dedicated customers we provide runbooks and we can support automated key rotation via KMS with a typical RTO within SLA windows; specific RTOs depend on the contract tier. We'll include the runbook excerpt in the pack.
[06:12] Marta (FinGuard): Let's talk about demo/test steps — to validate EU pinning we want a test where inference is provably processed in EU and logs show no egress. Can you do that?
[06:21] Liam (Redwood SE): Absolutely. We can provision a trial workspace in the EU region, run an inference with a unique trace id, and provide server-side logs and packet-flow evidence (private link logs). Priya will provision and run sample tests.
[06:34] John (FinGuard): Good. Also, can you provide a list of sub-processors with their regions? We need to map them against our policy.
[06:42] Alex (Redwood): We'll include the current list and the region mapping in the pack.
[06:47] Evan (FinGuard): Regarding backup retention and legal hold — we might need to put a legal hold and freeze deletion for certain accounts. Is that supported?
[06:54] Priya (Redwood SE): We have legal hold features for enterprise customers; we can pause deletion and extend retention. We'll add that to the runbook excerpt.
[07:02] Sana (FinGuard): On certification — SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are must-haves for us. Do you have those?
[07:08] Alex (Redwood): Yes we have SOC 2 Type II and are ISO 27001 aligned. We'll send the certification summarizes and attestations; some documents require an NDA for full reports.
[07:19] John (FinGuard): One more question: if you use any LLM models that have third-party licensing (open models from other providers), could that introduce cross-border issues? How do you manage model artifacts provenance?
[07:29] Priya (Redwood SE): We track model provenance. For EU-only requirements we can pin to model variants whose weights and artifacts are stored in EU. For some large-of-models there may be licensing constraints; we'll surface that in the model catalog.
[07:42] Marta (FinGuard): Sounds good. Can you also provide a timeline for pilot — we ideally want a 4-week pilot with EU pinning and a short run of our PII routing tests.
[07:51] Alex (Redwood): Yes 4-week pilot is reasonable. We'll provision EU trial by next week and you can run your tests.
[07:58] John (FinGuard): Great. Let's recap next steps.
[08:01] Alex (Redwood): Recap: 1) Alex will send security pack, SOC2 summary, and sub-processor list. 2) Priya will provision EU trial environment and run a verification inference with logs. 3) Martha -- sorry Marta will share workload/data class list that must remain in EU. 4) Evan will share DPA redlines. We'll schedule a tech deep-dive next week for the platform team to walk through runbooks and metrics.
[08:24] Evan (FinGuard): (laughs) we'll send the redlines.
[08:26] Alex (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and link to the pack -- security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/pack and SOC2 summary: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (placeholder links).
[08:36] John (FinGuard): Thanks all.
[08:38] Meeting end.
